'''Anadi Sankar Gupta''' (1 November 1932, [[Barisal]] – 14 June 2012, [[Kolkata]]) was an Indian mathematician.<ref name="statesman">{{cite news
 |url          = http://www.thestatesman.net/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&show=archive&id=413402&catid=72&year=2012&month=06&day=15
 |title        = Prof Anadi Shankar Gupta passes away
 |work         = [[The Statesman (India)|The Statesman]]
 |date         = 14 June 2012
 |access-date  = 24 June 2012
 |location     = [[Kolkata]]
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://archive.today/20130222091914/http://www.thestatesman.net/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&show=archive&id=413402&catid=72&year=2012&month=06&day=15
 |archive-date = 22 February 2013
 |df           = dmy-all
}}</ref> Till his death, he was an [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] Senior Scientist and [[emeritus|emeritus faculty]] with the Department of Mathematics, [[Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur|IIT Kharagpur]].<ref name="kgp_math">{{cite web
 |url=http://www.webmath.iitkgp.ernet.in/facultystaff.php
 |title=List of Faculty and Staff
 |publisher=Dept. of Mathematics, [[Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur|IIT Kharagpur]]
 |year=2004
 |access-date=22 March 2012
 |url-status=dead
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120607071349/http://www.webmath.iitkgp.ernet.in/facultystaff.php
 |archive-date=7 June 2012
}}</ref>

He was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology|Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]] for [[mathematical sciences]] in 1972 by the [[Government of India]] for his "significant contributions in the field of [[fluid dynamics]] and [[magnetohydrodynamics]], notably on [[heat transfer]] in [[natural convection|free convection]] flow in the presence of [[magnetic field]]," amongst other things.<ref name="ssb_citation">{{cite web
 |url          = http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/MATHEMATICAL_SCIENCES.htm
 |title        = Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Awards&nbsp;– Mathematical Sciences (1958–1998)
 |publisher    = [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]]
 |work         = (Citation)
 |access-date  = 22 March 2012
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120218182837/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/MATHEMATICAL_SCIENCES.htm
 |archive-date = 18 February 2012
 |df           = dmy-all
}}</ref>

==Life==
Anadi Sankar Gupta was born to Pramode Chandra and Usharani Gupta in Goila of [[Barisal District]] in the then [[British Raj|British India]] (present [[Bangladesh]]). He had his initial schooling at Domohani Kelejora High School in [[Asansol]], West Bengal. Gupta completed his [[Bachelor's degree|bachelors]] from [[Presidency University, Kolkata|Presidency College, Calcutta]] in 1952 and followed it up with a [[Master's degree|master's]] in [[applied mathematics]] from the [[University of Calcutta]] in 1954.<ref name="csir">{{cite book
| title=Bhatnagar Laureates (1958–91)
| publisher=[[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]]
| year=1992
| location=New Delhi
| pages=138–139}}</ref>

Prof. Gupta died in [[Kolkata]] on 14 June 2012 after suddenly taking ill.<ref name="statesman" />

==Academic career==
Gupta's [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctoral]] thesis was done under the supervision of G. Bandyopadhyay at the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur]] in 1958. He further acquired a [[Doctor of Science|D. Sc.]] from the same institute in 1966.

He joined the faculty of IIT Kharagpur in 1957 as an associate lecturer and rose through the ranks to become a professor and subsequently, an emeritus. He was President of the annual Congress of the [[Indian Mathematical Society]] in 1999.<ref name="statesman" /> He also served on the editorial boards of various scientific journals.<ref name="csir" /> He retired in 1993, but continued to be active in research.<ref name="statesman" />

===Research areas===
* [[Boundary layer|Boundary layer theory]]
* [[Heat transfer|Heat]] and [[mass transfer]] in fluid flows
* [[Hydrodynamic stability]]
* Stability of flows
